title: Trigonometric Integrals

methods.name: Odd power of sine or cosine
methods.summary: Split off one factor and turn the rest into the other function with \sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1.
steps: Peel off one factor of the odd-power function.
Rewrite the remaining even power with \sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1.
Substitute for the other function and integrate.

methods.name: Half-angle reduction of even powers
methods.summary: Lower an even power with \cos^2 x = \tfrac{1}{2}(1+\cos 2x) and \sin^2 x = \tfrac{1}{2}(1-\cos 2x).
steps: Replace each even power with the half-angle identity.
Expand and integrate term by term; repeat if a power remains.

conventions: Name the identity you use on the page.
Derivatives are written in Leibniz form, dy/dx.

pitfalls.description: Forgetting the factor 1/2 from the chain rule when integrating \cos 2x.
Leaving the peeled-off factor out of the substitution so that dw has no match.

subskills.name: Split an odd power
subskills.description: Peel off one factor and convert the rest with the Pythagorean identity.

subskills.name: Half-angle reduction
subskills.description: Lower an even power with the half-angle identities and integrate.

subskills.name: Pythagorean identity
subskills.description: Use \sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1 and its tan/sec form to rewrite an expression.
